criteria.justification: The response reframes the task as fixing the recurring pattern ('each label fixes one misunderstanding while creating another') rather than just picking a better name this round.
It explicitly proposes agreeing on 'who approves the choice, when the decision closes' and to 'ship on a set date,' treating continued indecision as costly rather than neutral.
The response sets a bar for reopening as 'a material customer misunderstanding, not a newly expressed preference,' explicitly separating substantive concerns from re-litigation.
It states 'the locked API field would remain unchanged, with its mapping to the customer-facing term documented,' directly incorporating the fixed constraint into the plan.

The response explains a process shift (testing full 'name plus description/UI context' treatments and documenting prior objections as constraints) rather than repeating a bare-name contest, but it never proposes or evaluates a concrete new candidate name to show the new process working in practice.
